title: Decode a PowerShell Attack
description: Use CyberChef to decode a Base64-encoded PowerShell reverse shell.
problemStatement:
### Scenario
You see the following suspicious PowerShell command line in your SIEM:

```
powershell.exe -NoP -NonI -W Hidden -Enc 
```

### Task
1.  Go to [CyberChef](https://gchq.github.io/CyberChef/).
2.  Use the **'From Base64'** recipe (and possibly **'Decode text'** with UTF-16LE encoding) to decode the string.
3.  Paste the decoded output into your answer.

### Questions
1.  What IP address and port is the script connecting to?
2.  What is the purpose of this script?
3.  What flags (`-NoP`, `-NonI`, `-W Hidden`, `-Enc`) indicate this is malicious?
hints: PowerShell Base64 uses Unicode (UTF-16LE) encoding. In CyberChef, after 'From Base64', add 'Decode text' with encoding 'UTF-16LE (1200)'.
Look for `New-Object System.Net.Sockets.TCPClient` in the decoded output.
expectedOutput: Decoded script text. Answers: 1. 192.168.1.100:4434. 2. Reverse shell giving attacker command line access. 3. -NoP (No Profile), -NonI (Non-Interactive), -W Hidden (Window Hidden), -Enc (Encoded Command).
